Hi Carlos / Veridian procurement team —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the specific asks we discussed so we can align next steps:

1) What we heard you say:
- You prefer a PO-based commercial path for enterprise purchases.
- You have a vendor onboarding packet (W-9, COI, vendor form) and legal review for new SaaS vendors.
- There may be a marketplace option but still under evaluation by your platform team.

2) Clarifying questions (can you confirm?):
- Vendor packet: who is the right person to receive our vendor packet (email/contact)?
- PO cadence & lead time: what is your typical PO issuance timeline once terms are agreed (days)?
- Card for pilot: would you accept corporate card for an initial pilot? If so, what is the threshold (dollar cap) and approval route?
- Any special billing requirements (invoice remittance address, AP contact, purchase order fields)?

3) Our proposed immediate next steps:
- I’ll share a short vendor-onboarding checklist and pilot pricing sheet (attached).
- If PO is the preferred route, can you share an example PO or your procurement template so we validate fields upfront?
- If card is acceptable for a pilot, we can offer a short-term card billing option and invoice the remainder after pilot.

Attachments: redwood_vendor_onboarding_checklist.pdf (vendor docs list), pilot-pricing-sheet.xlsx (pilot SKU & pricing)

Please reply with the AP contact and the PO/card preferences and estimated timelines. I’ll loop in our finance and CS leads to keep things moving.

Thanks,

Aditya — thanks for the clear recap. A few answers from procurement / finance side below: 

- Vendor packet: please send the complete packet to procurement@veridianbio.com. Our procurement coordinator (Lena Park) will own intake and follow-up.
- Required docs: W-9, signed vendor agreement (usually our legal team will propose edits), COI if applicable.
- PO lead time: typical turnaround is 7–14 business days after legal signoff; urgent requests can sometimes move faster but require procurement approval.
- Card for pilot: we can accept corporate card for POs under $3,500 but the request must be approved by our procurement coordinator; larger pilots require a PO.
- Marketplace: the IT/platform team is reviewing marketplace integrations; if the product is available through our approved marketplace we can do a faster procurement flow, but that’s TBD.

For planning: we’d prefer to proceed with a PO for a quarter-long pilot to keep everything on the books. If you can return the vendor packet and a sample PO or invoice format, Lena will create a vendor record and estimate the PO date range.

Attaching: Veridian_vendor_request_form.pdf (internal form)

Carlos Ruiz
Sr. Procurement Manager, Veridian Biotech
c.ruiz@veridianbio.com
